transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Eve Harper (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (CISO, Inkwell), Miguel Alvarez (Head of Infra), Tom Briggs (Legal), Priya Singh (Product)

Summary (auto):
Customer wants confirmation on EU/US region pinning, cross-border processing, and KMS options (BYOK vs Redwood-managed). Also asked about audit log retention, SOC2/ISO artifacts, RBAC & SSO integration, and subprocessors in US and EU. Next: security packet, subprocessor CSV, BYOK demo, DPA amendment conversation, 2-week pilot scope.

Topics: Data residency, region binding, KMS/BYOK, VPC/private deployment, subprocessor chain, audit logs and retention, legal/DPA items.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:00] Eve (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick round of intros; I'm Eve from Redwood, AE on this account.
[00:00:07] Laura (CISO): Hi, Laura Chen, CISO at Inkwell. We run the core payments and risk platform, so this is priority.
[00:00:12] Miguel (Infra): Miguel here, infra lead. We're interested in how your region binding and KMS will work with our EU customers.
[00:00:18] Tom (Legal): Tom Briggs, legal. We'll be focused on DPA and subprocessors.
[00:00:22] Priya (Product): Priya, product, owner of the pilot.
[00:00:25] Samir (SE): Samir Patel, Redwood SE -- I'll take the technical bits.
[00:00:28] Eve (AE): Cool. Quick agenda: review residency/regional binding, KMS options (BYOK vs Redwood-managed), audit logs and RBAC/SSO, and then next steps. Does that align?
[00:00:37] Laura: Yep, also timeline: we need production-ready answers for legal and compliance by mid-March if possible.
[00:00:42] Eve: Understood.

[00:01:05] Samir (SE): To start, at a high level Redwood supports three deployment modes: hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC deployment. For residency we offer region affinity and a region pinning policy that can enforce routing to EU regions for EU-labeled requests.
[00:01:18] Miguel: That's the part I want to unpack. Is region pinning a strict block or a soft affinity with fallback? What happens if capacity in eu-west-1 is saturated?
[00:01:27] Samir: Great question. You can choose strict pinning where requests are only routed to specified regions; if capacity is unavailable, requests fail with a specific error code. Alternatively, you can configure soft affinity with automatic fallback to a defined region set. For Inkwell we can set: primary eu-west-1, fallback eu-central-1, and emergency us-east-1 only after explicit approval and audit log flagging.
[00:01:46] Laura: We can't have silent failover to the US. Any cross-border processing must be explicit and logged, with SSO admin approval and legal notification.
[00:01:53] Samir: Totally reasonable — Redwood supports an allowlist policy plus a manual fallback workflow. When fallback is used it adds a metadata flag and creates an audit event. We can also require a JIRA ticket or an API toggle that only your admins can flip.

[00:02:30] Miguel: Ok, about data at rest — for EU customer data that you process in eu regions, is it encrypted with Redwood-managed keys or can we BYOK?
[00:02:38] Samir: Both. We offer Redwood KMS-managed keys for standard use and BYOK integrations where you can provide an external key in an HSM or use cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Google KMS) with a trust boundary. For private deployment we can integrate your KMS over a dedicated tunnel and import a wrapped key material.
[00:02:54] Laura: Do you support split-key schemes or dual-control escrow? Finance will want to know about key escrow and split control.
[00:03:01] Samir: We have an HSM-backed BYOK flow that supports key lifecycle controls and limited split-key patterns; full multi-party escrow is more of a legal/ops workflow we can implement for enterprise. We can document the sequence of Wrap/Unwrap, key rotation cadence, and our key usage policies.
[00:03:17] Tom: We'll need to see the KMS integration architecture diagram. Also clarifying: where are audit logs stored? EU logs must remain in EU for certain customers.
[00:03:25] Samir: Audit logs are configurable. For private and dedicated, logs can be retained in your VPC or a region you specify. For hosted, we can shard logs by region and provide EU-only retention for EU-labeled tenants; exported logs can be pushed to your S3/GCS bucket in eu-west.

[00:03:52] Laura: What about PII in logs — do you redact request/response payloads?
[00:03:56] Samir: By default we keep metadata and request hashes. You can opt into full payload logging for debugging, but we recommend token-level redaction. We have built-in filters to redact sequences that match patterns (account numbers, SSNs); customization is available for enterprise.

[00:04:20] Priya: For the pilot we'd like to test EU-only routing and BYOK with low-latency 99th percentile under 200ms. Is that feasible?
[00:04:27] Samir: Feasible for small-scale pilot; latency depends on model choice and instance size. We'll propose a config and run a 2-week pilot to measure tail latency. We can also provide per-token cost estimates for the two modes.

[00:04:58] Miguel: Subprocessors — can you give me the current list and which of them process data outside EU?
[00:05:04] Eve: We'll share the subprocessor CSV; quick sanity check: most infra subprocessors provide global presence, but we maintain a list of EU-only partners for zone-restricted deployments. We'll send the current inventory.
[00:05:13] Tom: Also need assurances that any cross-border egress is logged and subject to DPA clauses; and need to review your subprocessor onboarding process.
[00:05:20] Eve: Understood. We'll include the subprocessor onboarding policy in the packet and our standard flow for notifying customers of new subprocessors.

[00:05:45] Laura: Can you confirm certifications? SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001?
[00:05:50] Eve: Yes, we are SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certified. I'll attach redacted reports and the scope.
[00:05:55] Laura: Great. We'll need the scope doc showing EU control coverage.

[00:06:10] Samir: On RBAC and SSO — Redwood supports SAML2.0/Okta and OIDC for SSO, plus role-based access controls with per-token permissions. You can restrict who can flip fallback routing, who can import KMS keys, and who can export logs.
[00:06:23] Miguel: Do you support SCIM for provisioning?
[00:06:25] Samir: Yes, SCIM and attribute mapping. We can map groups to roles and enable MFA enforcement via IdP policies.

[00:06:40] Tom: About the DPA: we may want a clause that prohibits processing in non-EU regions except under documented emergency with legal signoff. Is that something Redwood is open to?
[00:06:49] Eve: Yes, we can negotiate DPA language around explicit emergency processing and audit trail requirements. We'll ask legal to provide template amendments.

[00:07:10] Miguel: Network topology: For private deployment, how does traffic flow? We want minimal egress and no internet traversal for EU data.
[00:07:18] Samir: For private VPC we operate a customer-controlled control plane; data path can be entirely internal to your VPC via private endpoints, no internet egress. For hosted, we have private networking options like PrivateLink and Customer-managed peering.
[00:07:33] Miguel: And what about KV cache / prefixes — are caches stored in region?
[00:07:36] Samir: Yes, KV cache is colocated with the serving tier in the same region as the request. We can configure cache TTL and replication behavior; for EU-only workloads we keep cache shards in EU regions. (transcription note: sometimes mentioned as "k v cash" in earlier notes)

[00:08:00] Laura: Can you show an example audit event when fallback to US happens?
[00:08:04] Samir: Example: event type = "region_fallback", timestamp, request_id, original_region=eu-west-1, executed_region=us-east-1, admin_approval_id=JIRA-1234, reason=capacity_rebalance. All events available through the audit API and streamed to your logging bucket.

[00:08:30] Priya: We also need to know about retention windows — both logs and model artifacts.
[00:08:34] Samir: Logs: configurable retention up to multi-year; can be exported daily. Model artifacts / KV: retained per config, but we recommend short TTLs for ephemeral caches and separate persistent stores for customer-owned artifacts.

[00:09:00] Tom: A legal question — do you offer contractual guarantees for data residency (i.e., region binding as a contractual SLO)?
[00:09:07] Eve: For enterprise contracts we can add residency commitments with remedies. It will vary by negotiation but yes, we can include region-binding SLOs in the contract.

[00:09:40] Laura: On encryption in transit, does Redwood terminate TLS in the region or at an edge? We need to ensure keys for TLS are in EU.
[00:09:48] Samir: TLS termination is regional for dedicated/private; for hosted we use edge termination with regional re-encryption; but we can offer regional TLS termination with certs managed by you or via your PKI for private deployments.

[00:10:10] Miguel: Any issues with HSM-backed KMS for high throughput? We have some strict latency budgets.
[00:10:15] Samir: Known overhead is KMS unwrap/verify on session start; we minimize round trips by caching decrypted session keys in region and using short-lived session keys. For high throughput models we recommend instance-level encryption keys to avoid per-token KMS calls.

[00:10:45] Eve: Quick check — timeline again: legal needs DPA language mid-March, pilot starts second week of March?
[00:10:52] Priya: If you're able to send security artifacts and the subprocessor list this week, we can aim for an internal sign-off and start pilot week of 2026-03-16.

[00:11:10] Samir: We'll prepare a pilot runbook: configs, model choice, load profile, test prompts, and measurement metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost). We'll also include the KMS BYOK steps and required access.

[00:11:35] Miguel: Is there a way to push audit logs in real time to our SIEM?
[00:11:39] Samir: Yes, realtime streaming via Kinesis/PubSub/LogForwarder; we can set up a connector to your SIEM and provide JSON schema for events.

[00:12:10] (brief cross talk)
[00:12:40] Laura: Are there any subprocessors we should be worried about in the US that might touch EU data?
[00:12:44] Eve: We have a handful of monitoring and analytics subprocessors in US; for EU-only customers we can limit to EU-hosted equivalents or self-hosted options. We'll mark those in the CSV.

[00:13:05] Tom: Will Redwood accept EU Standard Contractual Clauses or other SCCs for cross-border transfers?
[00:13:10] Eve: Yes, SCCs can be included with the DPA; we support them and also provide model clauses we use.

[00:13:40] Priya: About cost — are there meaningful cost differentials between BYOK private deployment and hosted EU-only?
[00:13:46] Samir: BYOK/private often has higher fixed costs (reserved capacity, network egress as applicable) but can reduce per-token costs by optimizing instance types. Hosted EU-only is lower entry cost but less isolation. We'll include cost models in the packet.

[00:14:20] Laura: For audit purposes we need immutable logs for admin actions. Can Redwood guarantee write-once logs?
[00:14:25] Samir: We support append-only storage with integrity checks and can push to your immutable S3 bucket with object lock; we can also provide hash chaining for tamper evidence.

[00:14:50] Miguel: Any sandbox for us to test SSO + SCIM provisioning?
[00:14:54] Samir: Yes, we'll spin up a sandbox tenant with SSO endpoints and provide SCIM test credentials. That will be part of the pilot runbook.

[00:15:20] Tom: On the point of notification for new subprocessors — what's the SLA for notifying customers? 30 days? 60 days?
[00:15:25] Eve: Standard is 30 days notice; for enterprise agreements we can negotiate extended notice or immediate notification depending on materiality.

[00:15:50] Laura: If we do a BYOK flow, can you show the key rotation procedures and certificates for compliance?
[00:15:56] Samir: Yes, we'll include rotation diagrams, rotation cadence options, and the API for rewrapping keys.

[00:16:10] Priya: Operational question — who in Redwood will be our direct technical contact during pilot?
[00:16:13] Eve: Samir will lead technical, and I'll coordinate account aspects. We'll also assign a CSM if you go into pilot.

[00:16:35] Miguel: Are there any performance benchmarks for EU-only vs cross-region?
[00:16:39] Samir: We have internal benchmarks; we'll share a tailored benchmark using the model and sequence lengths you expect. For EU-only the tail latency improves due to reduced network hops.

[00:17:05] (brief pause)
[00:17:20] Laura: Ok let's recap next steps.
[00:17:22] Eve: Recap: Eve to send security packet with SOC2/ISO certs and architecture diagrams; Samir to share subprocessor inventory and proposed region mapping; Samir to prepare BYOK demo and pilot runbook; Tom to return DPA change requests; Priya to finalize pilot success criteria. Anything to add?
[00:17:38] Tom: Also include the example audit event schema and sample logs.
[00:17:41] Samir: Will do. We'll add the schema and a sample event stream.

[00:18:05] Priya: If we can get those by next week we can aim for the pilot start on 16th.
[00:18:09] Eve: We'll hit those dates.

[00:18:30] (closing pleasantries)
[00:18:40] Eve: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet and calendar invites for the demo.
[00:18:45] Laura: Thanks.
[00:18:48] Miguel: Thanks.
[00:18:50] Tom: Bye.

[00:18:55] (meeting ends)
